subject: Re: Output ownership assignment & telemetry evidence request
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@acme.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@acme.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Output ownership assignment & telemetry evidence request

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for sending over the most recent MSA + Order Form. Our legal team flagged the output "assignment" language in Section 6.2 — specifically the clause that appears to grant Redwood a broad feedback/train license and a right to use customer outputs to retrain models. That's not acceptable for us in the current form.

Two asks to move forward:
1) Can you confirm whether Redwood intends to claim ownership of customer-generated outputs, or whether this is intended only as a limited feedback/license for service quality and safety?
2) We need a short sample export of telemetry and the kinds of logs you capture (token-level telemetry, prompt text retention window, and any derived telemetry) so our security team can run it through their pipeline. A redlined MSA would also help.

We're trying to finalize commercial sign-off this week so we can start pilot integrations in mid-July.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Maya
Maya Singh
Head of Legal Operations, Acme Systems

Attachment: acme_redline_v1.docx (redlines from Acme legal)

From: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
To: Maya Singh <maya@acme.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Output ownership assignment & telemetry evidence request

Maya — thanks, received. Looping in Laura (legal) and Ben (AE) so we can answer both the contract and commercial questions. Quick answers up front:

- Redwood does NOT take ownership of customer outputs. The intent of the clause is a limited feedback/license to improve the service (safety/quality), not assignment of title or rights in your content.
- We can provide a sanitized telemetry sample that removes customer-identifying data and example prompts (we'll include token-level metrics and retention windows).

Action items we will deliver by EOD tomorrow (Jul 2):
- Clean redline that narrows the feedback/license language to a scoped, non-exclusive license for the purposes of improving the service and safety fixes.
- Telemetry sample export with a README explaining retention and PII handling.

Laura — can you take point on the redline language? Ben, can you confirm pilot timing so we don't block the July integration?

Thanks,
Chloe
Chloe Martin
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Quoted original: "Attachment: acme_redline_v1.docx"

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai, Maya Singh <maya@acme.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 02 Jul 2025 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Output ownership assignment & telemetry evidence request

Maya / Chloe / Ben — attaching our counter-redline and a compact summary of changes. High level: we propose replacing the broad "assignment/ownership" text with a three-line clause that: 1) confirms customer retains all title to input and output, 2) grants Redwood a time-limited, non-exclusive, revocable feedback license solely to improve service safety and performance, and 3) prohibits Redwood from using customer outputs to create a model derivative that is productized and sold as a standalone model.

Key points in our redline (attached as acme_redline_v1_redline.docx):
- Narrowed "Feedback License" to analytics + safety fixes; removed any language that could be read as assignment.
- Added an explicit prohibition on training for a commercial, standalone Redwood model without customer opt-in; allowed aggregated, de-identified learning for system-level improvements.
- Telemetry: documented retention periods (30 days for full prompt traces, 90 days for aggregated telemetry) and optional longer retention under customer-configured telemetry policies.

Attached: acme_redline_v1_redline.docx; telemetry_sample_export.csv (sanitized tokens + metrics)

Maya, you'll see we left an optional checkbox in the Order Form for an "Extended telemetry & retrain opt-in" that customers can choose if they want Redwood to run targeted retraining using fully-deidentified material. If Acme wants zero chance of retraining we can provide a contract-level opt-out.

Please review and flag anything mission-critical. If acceptable, Ben — can you push the amended Order Form to DocuSign once Maya confirms? We'll keep the language as narrow as possible to protect both sides.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: acme_redline_v1_redline.docx; telemetry_sample_export.csv

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: Maya Singh <maya@acme.com>, chloe.martin@redwood.ai

Maya — thanks for the quick review. Two logistical items from the commercial side so we can keep the pilot timeline: 1) If Acme opts out of retrain/extended telemetry, there is a modest price uplift we need to apply to cover the increased isolation/config overhead. I'll send a short Order Form amendment reflecting the opt-out pricing. 2) Once you sign off on Laura's narrow language we'll generate the final DocuSign packet.

Questions for Acme: can you confirm the pilot start window (mid-July still OK?) and whether procurement needs a vendor questionnaire answered before countersignature? We have a SOC 2 Type II report and a short security packet I can drop into your procurement instance.

Chloe — I'm happy to host a 30-min sync with Maya and Acme procurement today if that helps unblock anything.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
